q: What is the minimum age to apply for a California instruction permit?
a: 15 and a half
d: 14 and a half
exp: California accepts permit applications from age 15 and a half.
src: dmv.ca.gov, Instruction and Learner's Permits; California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 2

q: How old must the licensed driver supervising a permit holder under 18 be?
a: 25 or older
d: 30 or older
exp: A minor practicing on a permit must be supervised by a California-licensed driver at least 25 years old.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 2; dmv.ca.gov, Teen Driver Roadmap

q: How many hours of supervised practice must a California teen complete before the drive test?
a: 40 hours, with at least 5 at night
b: 50 hours, with at least 10 at night
c: 30 hours, with at least 10 at night
d: 60 hours, with at least 15 at night
exp: Minors need 50 hours of supervised practice, and at least 10 of them must be at night.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 12814.6(a)(4); dmv.ca.gov, Teen Driver Roadmap

q: How long must a driver under 18 hold an instruction permit before taking the drive test?
a: At least 3 months
d: At least 12 months
exp: A minor must hold the permit for at least 6 months, or turn 18, before the drive test.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 12814.6(a)(1); California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 2

q: During the first 12 months with a provisional license, when may you not drive unless a qualified adult rides with you?
a: Between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m.
d: Between 9 p.m. and 5 a.m.
exp: For the first year, provisional drivers may not drive from 11 p.m. to 5 a.m. without a qualified adult.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 12814.6(b)(1)(A); California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 2

q: In the first 12 months of a provisional license, which passengers may you not carry without a qualified adult?
a: Passengers under 18
d: Passengers under 25
exp: Provisional drivers may not transport passengers under 20 unless a parent, guardian, licensed driver 25 or older, or instructor rides along.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 12814.6(b)(1)(B); California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 2

q: What score do you need to pass the California knowledge test?
a: 70 percent
d: 80 percent
exp: DMV sets the passing score for the knowledge test at 80 percent.

q: How many times may you attempt the knowledge test on one application?
a: Two
d: Five
exp: You get three attempts to pass before you must reapply and pay again.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 3; dmv.ca.gov, Driver's Licenses

q: May a California driver under 18 use a hands-free phone while driving?
a: No, only to make an emergency call
b: Yes, if the phone is mounted
c: Yes, on streets with speed limits of 25 mph or less
d: Yes, with a parent's written permission
exp: Drivers under 18 may not use any wireless device while driving, even hands-free, except for emergency calls.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 23124; California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 8

q: A new resident holds a valid driver's license from another state. What must that person pass to get a California license?
a: The vision test and the drive test
b: Nothing; the license is exchanged as is
c: The knowledge test and the drive test
d: The vision test and the knowledge test
exp: California requires new residents with an out-of-state license to pass the knowledge test, along with the vision test.

q: How many hours of driver training with a licensed instructor must a California teen complete?
a: 4 hours
d: 12 hours
exp: Teens need 6 hours of professional behind-the-wheel training from a licensed driving school.
src: dmv.ca.gov, Teen Driver Roadmap; Cal. Veh. Code 12814.6(a)(3)

q: When does a California teen's instruction permit become valid for practice driving?
a: When the instructor signs it at the first lesson
b: As soon as you pass the knowledge test at DMV
c: When the classroom course certificate is issued
d: When the parent signs the permit at the DMV office
exp: A minor must wait to use the permit until driver training starts and the instructor validates it.

q: What is the youngest age at which you can get a California provisional license?
a: 15 and a half
exp: Provisional licenses go to applicants at least 16 but under 18 who meet every other requirement.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 12814.6; California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 2

q: How much is the application fee for an original California Class C license?
exp: The original Class C application fee is $46 at any age.

q: How much does a Class C drive test retest cost in California?
exp: DMV charges $9 for each Class C drive test retest.

q: How long are a California license application and its fee valid?
a: 12 months
d: 24 months
exp: The application and fee are valid for 12 months after you apply.

q: A 16-year-old fails the knowledge test. How long must they wait to retake it?
a: 7 days, not counting the day of the failure
c: 14 days, not counting the day of the failure
d: 30 days
exp: Minors must wait seven days to retake a failed knowledge test, not including the day they failed.

q: A 17-year-old fails the drive test. How long must they wait to retake it?
a: 7 days, not counting the day of the failure
b: 14 days, not counting the day of the failure
d: 21 days
exp: Minors must wait 14 days to retake a failed drive test, not including the day of the failure.

q: What vision standard does DMV use for its screening?
a: 20/20 in each eye
d: 20/70 in each eye
exp: The screening standard is 20/40 with both eyes together, or 20/40 in one eye and at least 20/70 in the other.
src: dmv.ca.gov, Vision Impairment and DMV Requirements

q: You fail the DMV vision screening. What form will your eye doctor complete?
a: Certificate of Completion of Driver Education
d: SR 1 report
exp: DMV asks your eye doctor to complete a Report of Vision Examination, form DL 62.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 3; dmv.ca.gov, Vision Impairment and DMV Requirements

q: You pass the vision test only while wearing glasses. What happens?
a: You must retake the vision test every year
b: You get a corrective lenses restriction
c: You may drive only in daylight
d: You must take a second drive test
exp: Passing with corrective lenses puts a corrective lenses restriction on your license, so you must wear them to drive.

q: Who must sign a minor's California license application when parents share joint custody?
a: Both parents
c: Only the parent who lives with the minor
d: A notary instead of a parent
exp: When parents or guardians share joint custody, both must sign the minor's application.

q: What does a parent or guardian accept by signing a minor's license application?
a: Financial responsibility for the minor's driving
b: The duty to ride along on every trip
c: Payment of all of the minor's traffic fines for life
d: Responsibility for the minor's school attendance
exp: Signing the application means the parent or guardian accepts financial responsibility for the teen's driving.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Sections 2 and 10; dmv.ca.gov, Instruction and Learner's Permits

q: Which exception lets a provisional driver drive alone between 11 p.m. and 5 a.m. in the first year?
a: Driving a friend home, with a note from a parent
b: Driving for work, with a note from the employer
c: Driving to a party, with a note from a parent
d: Driving within 5 miles of home, with no note
exp: A work need is an exception if the teen carries a signed note from the employer confirming the job.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 2; Cal. Veh. Code 12814.6(b)(2)

q: A provisional driver has two at-fault collisions in the first year. What happens?
a: A six-month suspension and a year of probation
b: 30 days driving only with an adult 25 or older
c: 30 days driving only with an adult 21 or older
d: A 90-day suspension of the license
exp: Two at-fault collisions or convictions mean 30 days of driving only with a licensed adult at least 25.

q: A provisional driver has three at-fault collisions or convictions in the first year. What is the result?
a: A 30-day suspension and 6 months of probation
b: 30 days of driving only with an adult 25 or older
c: A one-year revocation and a new driver ed course
d: A 6-month suspension and 1 year of probation
exp: Three at-fault collisions, convictions or a mix bring a six-month suspension and one year of probation.

q: A provisional driver in the first 12 months wants to drive a 17-year-old friend. Who must also be in the car to make the trip legal?
a: A licensed driver who is 25 or older
b: A licensed driver who is 21 or older
d: A licensed sibling who is 20 or older
exp: The limit lifts only when a parent, guardian, licensed driver 25 or older, or licensed instructor rides along.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 12814.6(b)(1); dmv.ca.gov, Teen Driver Roadmap

q: At what age can you get a California instruction permit without driver education or driver training certificates?
a: 16, with no drive test until 17 and a half
b: 15 and a half, if a parent signs the form
c: 17, with no drive test until you turn 18
d: 17 and a half, with no drive test until 18
exp: From 17 and a half, a permit can be issued without the certificates, but the drive test waits until you are 18.

q: Can a first-time applicant take the California permit knowledge test online at home?
a: Yes, through the DMV eLearning course
b: Yes, if you are 18 or older
c: Yes, if a parent proctors it at home
d: No, first-timers test at a DMV office
exp: DMV's online eLearning option is for license renewals; original applicants take the knowledge test in an office.
src: dmv.ca.gov, Online Learning; dmv.ca.gov, Instruction and Learner's Permits

q: In how many languages does DMV offer the knowledge test?
a: English only
d: More than 40
exp: DMV offers the knowledge test in more than 40 languages.

q: Who may ride with you during the California drive test?
a: Only the examiner
d: A driving instructor
exp: Only the examiner may be in the car, with exceptions for training, service animals and some law enforcement situations.

q: Which feature must be turned off during the California drive test?
a: Automated parallel parking
d: The daytime running lights
exp: Advanced driver assistance systems such as automated parking, lane departure and adaptive cruise control are not permitted on the test.

q: During the pre-drive check, how many rearview mirrors must your car have?
a: At least two, one on the left side
b: At least one, inside the car
d: At least two, both inside the car
exp: The car needs at least two rearview mirrors, and one must be on the left side.

q: If you use a rental car for the drive test, what is required?
a: A rental agent must ride along during the test
b: Rental cars are not allowed for the drive test
c: You must be on the contract, and it must allow drive tests
d: The renter must be 25 and ride to the office with you
exp: A rental car may be used only if you are listed on the contract and it does not exclude drive tests.

q: Who must accompany an applicant with a foreign driver's license to and from the drive test?
a: A certified interpreter
d: A licensed driver
exp: DMV requires an accompanying driver for applicants with a valid license from another country.

q: Which tests must a person with a license from another country pass to get a California license?
a: The vision and knowledge tests
c: No tests, if the license is valid
d: The vision, knowledge and drive tests
exp: California has no license exchange with other countries, so foreign license holders take the knowledge and drive tests too.

q: Within how many days of becoming a California resident must you get a California license?
a: 30 days
d: 10 days
exp: A new resident may drive on an out-of-state license for no more than 10 days after establishing residence.

q: What does a California license issued under AB 60 state on the card?
a: That the holder may not drive at night
b: That it is not valid for federal purposes
c: That it is valid only inside California
d: That the holder must carry a passport
exp: Licenses issued under AB 60 carry a notice that they are not acceptable for official federal purposes.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 12801.9; dmv.ca.gov, AB 60 Driver's Licenses

q: What tests must an AB 60 license applicant pass?
a: A vision test and the drive test
b: A special knowledge test in English
c: The same tests as every other applicant
d: No tests, if they drove in another country
exp: AB 60 applicants meet the same licensing requirements, including the knowledge and drive tests.
src: dmv.ca.gov, AB 60 Driver's Licenses; Cal. Veh. Code 12801.9

q: In California, is a REAL ID license required to drive?
a: Yes, for every driver after the federal deadline
b: Yes, for drivers under 18 on a first license
c: No; it is for flights and federal buildings
d: No; it is needed only for international travel
exp: REAL ID is optional for driving; it matters for boarding domestic flights and entering most federal facilities.

q: What do adults 18 or older skip compared with teen applicants?
a: The knowledge test and the vision test
b: The drive test, if they have driven before
c: Driver ed, driver training and the 6-month wait
d: The permit; adults go straight to the drive test
exp: Adults still take the vision, knowledge and drive tests but do not need driver education, training or the 6-month hold.
src: dmv.ca.gov, Instruction and Learner's Permits; dmv.ca.gov, Driver's Licenses

q: Which of these is a critical driving error that fails the California drive test?
a: The examiner has to intervene to prevent danger
b: Turning the steering wheel hand over hand
c: Waiting at a green light for a pedestrian to finish crossing
d: Checking a blind spot before a lane change
exp: Any action that requires the examiner to step in, by word or action, is a critical driving error.
src: dmv.ca.gov, Driving Performance Evaluation (DPE) Scoring Criteria

q: During the drive test, you drive 10 mph under the limit with no reason. How is it scored?
a: As a minor deduction only
d: It is not scored
exp: Driving 10 mph over or under the limit when conditions do not call for it is a critical driving error.
src: dmv.ca.gov, Driving Performance Evaluation (DPE) Scoring Criteria

q: What is the minimum age of the licensed driver supervising a permit holder who is 18 or older?
exp: Adults practice with a California-licensed driver at least 18; minors need one at least 25.

q: Unless posted otherwise, what is the California speed limit within 500 feet of a school while children are present?
a: 15 mph
d: 25 mph
exp: The default school zone limit is 25 mph within 500 feet of a school while children are present.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 7; Cal. Veh. Code 22352

q: A California city posts SPEED LIMIT 20 WHEN FLASHING in a school zone. When does the 20 mph limit apply?
a: From 7 a.m. to 4 p.m. on school days
b: When children are in the crosswalk
d: At all times
exp: Local 20 mph school zone limits apply under the condition shown on the sign, such as when the beacons flash.

q: In a California highway work zone with workers present, what happens to traffic fines?
a: They rise by a flat $35
d: They are doubled
exp: Fines are doubled in highway construction or maintenance zones when workers are present.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 7; Cal. Veh. Code 42009

q: What is a California Safety Enhanced Double Fine Zone?
a: A road where fines double due to serious crashes
b: A freeway zone where trucks pay double fines
c: A work zone where workers are present
d: A school zone during school hours
exp: Certain roads with more serious collisions are posted as Safety Enhanced Double Fine Zones, where fines are doubled.

q: What is the maximum fine for assaulting a highway worker in California?
exp: Anyone convicted of assaulting a highway worker faces fines up to $2,000 and up to one year in jail.

q: How should you merge when cones close a lane in a California work zone?
a: Merge early, without crossing the cones
b: Wait until the last cone, then cut in
c: Use the shoulder to get past the closed lane
d: Stop and wait for a flagger every time
exp: Merge as soon as it is safe and never cross the cones or drums that guide you.

q: In California, may you turn right on a steady red light?
a: No, California bans right turns on red
b: Yes, after a full stop, unless a sign forbids it
c: Yes, without stopping if no one is coming
d: Yes, after a full stop, where a sign allows it
exp: Right turns on red are legal after a complete stop and yielding, unless a sign forbids them.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 21453(b); California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 6

q: You are stopped at a red arrow pointing right. What does California law allow?
a: A right turn after a full stop
b: A right turn if no pedestrians are present
c: A right turn only if no traffic is coming from the left
d: No turn; wait for a green light or green arrow
exp: A red arrow means you may not turn in that direction until a green light or green arrow appears.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 21453(d); California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 6

q: When may you turn left on a red light in California?
a: From a one-way onto a two-way street, after stopping
b: From any street onto a one-way street, after stopping
c: From a two-way onto a one-way street, after stopping
d: From a one-way onto a one-way street, after stopping
exp: A left turn on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto another one-way street, unless a sign prohibits it.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 21453(b); California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 6

q: Where must you stop before turning right on red in California?
a: Just past the limit line, before the crosswalk
b: Past the crosswalk, where you can see cross traffic
c: At the limit line, or before the crosswalk if none
d: At the corner, even if a limit line is painted
exp: Stop behind the limit line; with no limit line, stop before the crosswalk, and with no crosswalk, before the intersection.

q: Turning left on red from a one-way street onto a one-way street, whom must you yield to?
a: Pedestrians and vehicles that have a green light
c: Pedestrians in the crosswalk, but not cars
d: Vehicles turning from the cross street
exp: Yield to pedestrians, bicyclists and vehicles with a green light, then turn when safe.

q: Under California's Move Over law, which stopped vehicles require you to move over or slow down?
a: Police cars and ambulances, but not tow trucks
b: Emergency vehicles, but not cars with hazard lights on
c: Emergency, tow and road crew vehicles, and cars with hazards
d: Any vehicle parked on a freeway shoulder, lights or not
exp: The law covers stopped emergency, tow and maintenance vehicles with warning lights, and any stopped vehicle showing hazard lights or warning devices.

q: You approach a stopped tow truck with flashing amber lights and cannot safely change lanes. What must you do?
a: Keep your speed and stay in your lane
b: Stop completely until the tow truck leaves
c: Slow to a reasonable and safe speed
d: Honk, then pass at your current speed
exp: If a lane change is unsafe or impractical, the Move Over law requires you to slow to a safe speed.

q: How close may you follow a fire engine or ambulance using its siren or flashing lights in California?
a: No closer than 100 feet
d: No closer than 1,000 feet
exp: It is illegal to follow within 300 feet of an emergency vehicle using its siren or flashing lights.

q: A school bus ahead on a two-lane road flashes red lights. What must California drivers in both directions do?
a: Slow to 15 mph and pass with care
b: Stop if children are visible, then go
c: Stop until the children are off the road
d: Stop until the red lights stop flashing
exp: Drivers from either direction must stop and remain stopped while the red lights flash.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 22454; California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 7

q: You are on a highway with two lanes in each direction. A school bus on the other side flashes red lights. What must you do?
a: Stop until the lights stop flashing
d: Proceed with care; you need not stop
exp: On a divided or multilane highway with two or more lanes each way, you do not stop for a bus on the other side.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 22454(b); California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 7

q: What do flashing yellow lights on a California school bus mean?
a: Children are crossing; stop now at any distance
b: The bus is turning; pass it on the left
c: The bus is about to stop; slow and get ready
d: The bus is stopped; pass slowly with care
exp: Flashing yellow lights warn that the bus is about to stop to let children off.

q: What can happen if you pass a California school bus with its red lights flashing?
a: A fine up to $1,000 and a possible one-year suspension
b: A fine up to $500 and a possible six-month suspension
c: A fine up to $250 and one point, but no suspension
d: A fine up to $1,000, but no suspension
exp: Failing to stop can mean a fine up to $1,000 and suspension of your driving privilege for one year.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 7; Cal. Veh. Code 22454.5

q: How far from a stopped school bus with red lights flashing must you stop under California law?
a: No set distance; stop before you reach it
b: At least 10 feet, as in most states
c: At least 50 feet from the bus
d: At least 20 feet from the stop arm
exp: California law requires a stop immediately before passing the bus but sets no minimum distance.

q: In a California residential district, when may you make a U-turn?
a: When no vehicle is approaching within 100 feet
b: When no vehicle is approaching within 200 feet
c: At a traffic light, but not mid-block
d: When no vehicle is within 50 feet of you
exp: A U-turn in a residential district is legal if no vehicles are approaching within 200 feet.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 6; Cal. Veh. Code 22103

q: Where is a U-turn always illegal in California?
a: In front of a fire station
c: At an intersection on a green light with no sign
d: Through a divided highway opening
exp: Never make a U-turn in front of a fire station or use its driveway to turn around.

q: In a California business district, where may you make a U-turn?
a: Anywhere the street is wide and traffic is light
b: From the right lane, after signaling
c: At an intersection or a divided highway opening
d: Mid-block, if no sign forbids it
exp: In business districts, U-turns are allowed only at intersections or at openings in a divided highway.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 6; Cal. Veh. Code 22102

q: May you make a U-turn in California if you cannot see 200 feet in each direction?
a: No
d: Yes, at night with headlights on
exp: Never make a U-turn when you cannot see clearly for 200 feet in each direction.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 6; Cal. Veh. Code 22105

q: May you make a U-turn across a single set of double yellow lines in California?
a: Yes, where it is otherwise legal
b: No, a double yellow may not be crossed
c: Yes, in a business district mid-block
d: No, unless a police officer waves you on
exp: The handbook allows a U-turn across a double yellow line, but not across two sets of double yellow lines.

q: How far before a turn must you signal in California?
a: At least 50 feet
d: At least 500 feet
exp: Signal at least 100 feet before you turn.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 5; Cal. Veh. Code 22108

q: How long before changing lanes on a California freeway should you signal?
a: At least two seconds
d: At least five seconds
exp: Signal at least five seconds before a lane change on a freeway.

q: When exiting a California highway, how early should you signal?
a: About two seconds, or 100 feet, before it
b: About one minute, or a mile, before it
c: About five seconds, or 400 feet, before it
d: About ten seconds, or 1,000 feet, before it
exp: Once in the proper lane, signal about five seconds, or roughly 400 feet, before you exit.

q: Unless posted otherwise, what is the maximum speed limit on most California highways?
a: 55 mph
d: 65 mph
exp: The maximum speed on most California highways is 65 mph unless a higher limit is posted.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 22349(a); California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 8

q: What is the California speed limit on a two-lane undivided highway, unless posted higher?
a: 45 mph
d: 50 mph
exp: Two-lane undivided highways have a 55 mph limit unless a higher limit is posted.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 22349(b); California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 8

q: What is the California speed limit when towing a trailer?
a: 55 mph
d: 65 mph
exp: Vehicles towing trailers are limited to 55 mph.

q: Unless posted otherwise, what is the speed limit in a California business or residential district?
a: 20 mph
d: 35 mph
exp: Business and residence districts have a 25 mph limit unless posted otherwise.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 22352; California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 7

q: What is the speed limit in a California alley?
a: 10 mph
d: 25 mph
exp: The speed limit in any alley is 15 mph.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 22352; California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 7

q: What is the speed limit at a California blind intersection?
a: 5 mph
d: 25 mph
exp: An intersection without stop signs where your view is blocked has a 15 mph limit.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 22352; California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 7

q: When is the speed limit 15 mph within 100 feet of a California railroad crossing?
a: At every crossing, whether or not you can see
b: When the crossing has no gates or signals
c: When a train is in sight within 1,000 feet
d: When you cannot see 400 feet along the tracks
exp: The 15 mph limit applies when you cannot see 400 feet both ways, unless gates, signals or a flagger control the crossing.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 22352; California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 7

q: What does California's Basic Speed Law say?
a: Drive at the posted limit when the road is clear
b: Never drive faster than is safe for conditions
c: Never drive slower than 45 mph on a highway
d: The posted limit is safe in every condition
exp: The Basic Speed Law forbids driving faster than is safe for conditions, whatever the posted limit.

q: What following distance rule does the California handbook teach?
a: The one-second rule
d: One car length per 20 mph
exp: Use at least three seconds to keep a safe distance from the vehicle ahead.

q: A tailgater is close behind you in California. What should you do with the space in front of you?
a: Tap your brakes, then keep the same gap
b: Speed up to open space behind you
c: Increase it, then let the driver pass
d: Close it so no one can cut in
exp: Create more space ahead when tailgated, then move right when safe and let the driver pass.

q: When merging onto a California highway, how much space should you leave ahead of you?
a: One second
d: Three seconds
exp: Leave three seconds of space between you and the vehicle in front when you merge.

q: How is a California carpool (HOV) lane marked on the pavement?
a: With a white arrow and the words BUS ONLY
b: With a circle and the words HOV ONLY
c: With yellow arrows pointing both ways
d: With a diamond and the words CARPOOL LANE
exp: HOV lanes are marked with a diamond symbol and the words Carpool Lane.

q: How do you know how many people you need to use a California HOV lane?
a: Posted signs show the minimum
b: It is two people on every HOV lane
c: It is three people at rush hour
d: It depends on how many seats your car has
exp: Signs at the on-ramp or along the road give the minimum occupancy and the hours it applies.

q: May you cross double solid white lines to enter a California HOV lane?
a: Yes, if you signal and it is safe
b: Yes, outside the posted HOV hours
c: No, use only the marked openings
d: Yes, if the HOV lane is moving slowly
exp: Never cross double solid lines into or out of an HOV lane; use the designated entrances and exits.

q: Can a solo driver use a California HOV lane today by displaying a clean air vehicle decal?
a: No; the decal program has ended
b: Yes, at any hour of the day
d: Yes, if the decal has not expired
exp: The federal authorization ended, so clean air vehicle decals are invalid and solo drivers must follow occupancy rules.
src: dmv.ca.gov, Federal Government Ends Clean Air Vehicle (CAV) Decal Program

q: May a motorcycle use a California HOV lane with only the rider aboard?
a: No, a passenger is required
b: Yes, if it has a clean air decal
c: No, not during posted HOV hours
d: Yes, unless signs say otherwise
exp: Motorcycles may use HOV lanes unless signs prohibit it.

q: How close to a fire hydrant may you park in California?
a: No closer than 5 feet
d: No closer than 30 feet
exp: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire hydrant.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 22514; California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 6

q: Under California law, how close may you park to the approach side of a crosswalk with no curb extension?
a: No closer than 10 feet
d: No closer than 20 feet
exp: Parking is banned within 20 feet of the approach side of any marked or unmarked crosswalk, or 15 feet where a curb extension exists.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 22500(n); California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 6

q: How close to a sidewalk ramp for disabled persons may you park in California?
a: No closer than 3 feet
d: No closer than 15 feet
exp: Never park within three feet of a sidewalk ramp for disabled persons.

q: How close to the nearest railroad rail may you park in California?
a: No closer than 7 and a half feet
b: No closer than 3 and a half feet
d: No closer than 12 and a half feet
exp: No vehicle may park on a railroad track or within 7 and a half feet of the nearest rail.

q: When parallel parking in California, how close must your wheels be to the curb?
a: Within 18 inches
d: Within 36 inches
exp: Park with your right-hand wheels parallel to and within 18 inches of the curb.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 22502; California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 6

q: What does a red curb mean in California?
a: Loading of passengers or freight
d: No stopping, standing or parking
exp: A red curb means no stopping, standing or parking; buses may stop at a red zone marked for buses.

q: What does a white curb mean in California?
a: Parking for disabled placards only
d: Parking for a limited time, often 30 minutes
exp: At a white curb, stop only to load or unload passengers.

q: What does a green curb mean in California?
a: Parking for a limited time
d: No parking at any time
exp: A green curb allows parking for a limited time, shown on a sign or painted on the curb.

q: What does a yellow curb mean in California?
a: Parking for the limited time shown on the sign
b: No stopping, standing or parking at any time
c: Parking for disabled placards or plates only
d: Loading passengers or freight, for the posted time
exp: A yellow curb is a loading zone for passengers and freight, limited to the posted time.

q: Who may park at a blue curb in California?
a: Anyone, for up to 15 minutes while loading passengers
b: Disabled people or their drivers, with a placard or plate
c: Electric vehicles while they are plugged in to charge
d: Commercial vehicles loading freight
exp: Blue curbs are for disabled persons or drivers of disabled persons with a placard or special plate.

q: How close to a fire station driveway may you park in California?
a: No closer than 5 feet
d: No closer than 50 feet
exp: Do not park within 15 feet of a fire station driveway.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 22500(d); California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 6

q: Under California law, what is the minimum space when passing a bicyclist in the same lane?
a: 2 feet
d: 6 feet
exp: You must leave at least three feet between your car and the bicyclist when passing.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 21760; California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 7

q: Another lane in your direction is open as you approach a bicyclist in your lane. What does California law require?
a: Pass in the same lane at 3 feet
b: Pass in the same lane if you can give 4 feet
c: Change lanes to pass, when it is safe
d: Follow the cyclist until the road widens
exp: If another same-direction lane is available, you must change lanes to pass when safe and practical.

q: You cannot give a California bicyclist 3 feet of space. What should you do?
a: Pass quickly with less space
b: Slow down and wait to pass until you can
c: Pass with less space after sounding your horn
d: Pass at your normal speed if the cyclist stays right
exp: If you cannot give three feet, do not pass until you can; slow to a safe speed.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 7; Cal. Veh. Code 21760(d)

q: How close to a turn may you enter a bike lane to turn right in California?
a: No more than 50 feet before the turn
b: No more than 500 feet before the turn
c: No more than 200 feet before the turn
d: You may never enter a bike lane
exp: You may drive in a bike lane within 200 feet of a turn, after checking for bicyclists.

q: Within how many days must you report a California collision to DMV on the SR 1 form when required?
a: 24 hours
d: 10 days
exp: The SR 1 report goes to DMV within 10 days when a crash causes injury, death or over $1,000 in property damage.

q: California requires a DMV report of a collision when property damage to any one person is more than what amount?
exp: A report is required when property damage exceeds $1,000, or when anyone is injured or killed.

q: A California collision injures someone. Within how long must the driver report it to the CHP or city police?
a: 1 hour
d: 24 hours
exp: A crash with injury or death must be reported in writing to the CHP or city police within 24 hours.

q: How close to an oncoming vehicle may you keep your high beams on in California?
a: Dim them within 200 feet
d: Dim them within 500 feet
exp: Switch to low beams within 500 feet of a vehicle coming toward you.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 5; Cal. Veh. Code 24409

q: When following another vehicle in California, within what distance must you dim your high beams?
a: 300 feet
d: 1,000 feet
exp: Dim your high beams within 300 feet of a vehicle you are following.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 5; Cal. Veh. Code 24409

q: What is the legal BAC limit for a California driver 21 or older?
a: 0.05 percent
d: 0.04 percent
exp: It is illegal for a driver 21 or older to drive with a BAC of 0.08 percent or higher.

q: What is the legal BAC limit for a California driver under 21?
a: 0.02 percent
d: 0.01 percent
exp: Drivers under 21 may not drive with a BAC of 0.01 percent or higher.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 9; Cal. Veh. Code 23136

q: What is the BAC limit for a California driver on DUI probation?
a: 0.04 percent
d: 0.01 percent
exp: A driver on DUI probation may not drive with a BAC of 0.01 percent or higher, at any age.

q: What is the BAC limit for a California driver carrying passengers for hire?
a: 0.01 percent
d: 0.08 percent
exp: Driving passengers for hire, or a vehicle that needs a commercial license, sets the limit at 0.04 percent.

q: A California driver under 21 tests at 0.01 percent BAC. What happens to the license?
a: It is suspended for one year
d: The driver gets a warning
exp: Under 21 with a BAC of 0.01 or higher, the driving privilege is suspended for one year.

q: What happens the first time a California driver 21 or older refuses a chemical test after a DUI arrest?
a: A 30-day suspension
d: A ten-year revocation
exp: A first refusal brings a one-year suspension of the driving privilege.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 13353(a)(1); dmv.ca.gov, Driving Under the Influence

q: A California driver refuses a chemical test a second time within 10 years. What is the penalty?
a: A one-year suspension
d: A two-year revocation
exp: A second refusal within 10 years brings a two-year revocation.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 13353(a)(2); dmv.ca.gov, Driving Under the Influence

q: After a California DUI arrest, how long do you have to request a DMV hearing?
a: 24 hours from the arrest
d: 10 days from the arrest
exp: You may request a DMV administrative hearing within 10 days of the arrest.

q: After a California DUI arrest, the officer takes your license. How long is the temporary license you may receive?
a: 10 days
d: One year
exp: The officer may give you a temporary license valid for 30 days.

q: A driver 21 or older tests at 0.08 percent for a first offense. What immediate DMV action follows?
a: A one-month suspension
d: No action until a court conviction
exp: Under Administrative Per Se, a first offense at 0.08 or higher brings a four-month suspension.

q: What is the fine range for a first DUI conviction in California?
exp: A first DUI conviction carries a fine of $390 to $1,000 plus jail of 96 hours to six months.

q: How long does a California DUI conviction stay on your driving record?
a: 3 years
d: Permanently
exp: All DUI convictions remain on your driver's record for 10 years.

q: Where may an opened container of alcohol be carried in a California car?
a: In the glove box
d: In a passenger's hand
exp: An opened container must be kept in the trunk, or where passengers do not sit; never in the glove box.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 23225; California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 9

q: In which vehicle may a passenger legally hold an open alcohol container in California?
a: A friend's car
d: A taxi
exp: The open container rule does not apply to passengers in a bus, taxi, camper or motorhome.

q: May an adult California driver hold a phone while driving?
a: Yes, while stopped at a red light in traffic
c: No; it must be mounted or used hands-free
d: Yes, below 25 mph
exp: Adults may not hold and operate a phone while driving; a mounted phone may be used with a single swipe or tap.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 23123.5; California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 8

q: Where may a California driver mount a phone?
a: On the steering wheel hub, facing the driver
b: In a cup holder or on the passenger seat
c: On the dash, windshield or console, clear of the view
d: Anywhere in the car, if it does not block the view
exp: The phone may be mounted on the windshield, dashboard or center console if it does not block the view of the road.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 23123.5(c); California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 8

q: What is the base fine for a first California handheld phone violation?
exp: The base fine is $20 for a first offense and $50 for each later one.

q: When does a California handheld phone violation add a point to your record?
a: On a repeat conviction within 36 months
b: On every conviction, including the first
c: On a repeat conviction within 12 months
d: On a third conviction within 5 years
exp: A point is added for a phone violation within 36 months of a prior conviction for the same offense.

q: In California, who gets the ticket if a 14-year-old passenger is not wearing a seat belt?
a: The driver
d: Both the driver and the passenger
exp: The driver can be ticketed for any unbelted passenger under 16.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 8; Cal. Veh. Code 27360.5

q: Which passengers must wear seat belts in California?
a: Front seat passengers
d: Everyone, when on a freeway
exp: You and all your passengers must be belted; passengers 16 and older are personally responsible.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 8; Cal. Veh. Code 27315

q: How must a California child under 2 ride?
a: Forward facing, once over 20 pounds
b: In a forward-facing seat in the back
c: Rear facing until age 1, then forward facing
d: Rear facing, unless at least 40 pounds or 40 inches
exp: Children under 2 ride rear facing unless they weigh at least 40 pounds or are at least 40 inches tall.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 27360(b); California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 8

q: Where must a California child under 8 usually ride?
a: In the front seat with a regular belt
b: In any seat, with a regular safety belt
c: In a booster in the front passenger seat
d: In a car seat or booster in a rear seat
exp: Children under 8 ride in a child restraint in a rear seat, with a few listed exceptions.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 27360(a); California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 8

q: When may a California child use a regular safety belt instead of a car seat or booster?
a: At 8, or 4 feet 9 inches, if the belt fits
b: At 6, or 4 feet tall, if the belt fits
c: At 40 pounds, or 40 inches, if the belt fits
d: At 10, or 5 feet tall, if the belt fits
exp: Children 8 or older, or at least 4 feet 9 inches tall, may use a safety belt; the belt must fit correctly (back against the seat, knees bent at the edge, shoulder belt across the chest, lap belt low on the thighs).
src: Cal. Veh. Code 27363, 27360.5 (AB 435, operative January 1, 2027); California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 8

q: Under California law, a child of what age may not be left alone in a car without a supervisor 12 or older?
a: 10 or younger
d: 6 or younger
exp: It is illegal to leave a child 6 or younger unattended unless someone at least 12 supervises.

q: What minimum liability insurance must California car owners carry for injury or death of one person?
exp: Minimum coverage is $30,000 for one person, $60,000 per crash and $15,000 for property damage.

q: What is California's minimum property damage liability coverage?
exp: California requires at least $15,000 of property damage liability coverage.

q: When must you turn on your headlights in California?
a: From sunset to sunrise, but not in daytime
b: When driving above 55 mph in daylight
c: Whenever the road surface is wet
d: Whenever your wipers are in continuous use
exp: Headlights are required in darkness, when you cannot see 1,000 feet, and when wipers run continuously.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 24400; California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 5

q: Within how many days must you tell California DMV about a new address?
a: 30 days
d: 10 days
exp: Notify DMV of your new address within ten days.

q: Is it legal in California to drive wearing earbuds in both ears?
a: Yes, at low volume
d: Yes, if the volume lets you hear sirens
exp: It is illegal to wear a headset or earplugs in both ears while driving.

q: Is it legal to smoke in a California car when a minor is inside?
a: Yes, with a window open
c: Yes, if the car is parked
d: Yes, if the minor agrees
exp: Smoking with a minor in the vehicle is illegal and can bring a fine.

q: What happens first on the California drive test?
a: A merge onto a nearby freeway
b: A parallel parking test at the curb
c: A check of the car and its controls
d: A backing test in the parking lot
exp: The examiner first has you locate and show the car's controls and checks that it is safe.

q: During the California drive test, you roll through a stop sign faster than a brisk walk. What is the result?
a: A minor error that costs a few points
b: A critical driving error that fails the test
c: A warning, unless another car was near
d: Nothing, if no car or person was coming
exp: Disobeying a sign, such as exceeding a brisk walking speed at a stop sign, is a critical driving error.
src: dmv.ca.gov, Driving Performance Evaluation (DPE) Scoring Criteria

q: During the California drive test, you drive more than 200 feet in a center left turn lane. How is it scored?
a: As correct use of the turn lane
b: As a minor error, a few points off
d: As an error only if a car is near
exp: Driving more than 200 feet in a bike lane or center left turn lane is a lane violation and a critical error.
src: dmv.ca.gov, Driving Performance Evaluation (DPE) Scoring Criteria

q: May you use a backup camera during the California drive test?
a: No, it must be covered or turned off
b: Yes, but you must still look over your shoulder
c: Yes, and it replaces looking over your shoulder
d: Yes, but only when parking, not backing
exp: Safety technology such as backup cameras may be used, but it does not replace visual checks.

q: Your car's tire is a spare donut on drive test day in California. What happens?
a: The test is rescheduled
d: You may test if you drive slowly
exp: A donut tire is not allowed, and a car that fails the pre-drive check means the test is rescheduled.

q: How many drive test attempts does one California application allow?
a: One
d: Unlimited
exp: The application fee covers three drive test attempts; after three failures you reapply.

q: During the California drive test, it starts to rain and you do not turn on your wipers. How is that scored?
a: It is not scored, since weather is not part of the route
d: As a critical error only if the examiner has to remind you
exp: Failing to use wipers, defroster or headlights when conditions require them is a critical driving error.
src: dmv.ca.gov, Driving Performance Evaluation (DPE) Scoring Criteria

q: Who certifies a California teen's 50 hours of supervised practice?
a: A parent or guardian
d: The insurance company
exp: A parent or guardian certifies the practice hours and that the teen is ready for the drive test.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 12814.6(a)(4); California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 2

q: Do night hours count toward a California teen's 50 practice hours?
a: No, the 10 night hours come on top of the 50
b: Yes, and at least 10 must be at night
c: Yes, but at most 5 night hours count
d: Only if driven with an instructor
exp: The 10 night hours are part of the 50-hour total.
src: Cal. Veh. Code 12814.6(a)(4); dmv.ca.gov, Teen Driver Roadmap

q: What standard program length does California use for classroom driver education?
a: 10 hours
d: 50 hours
exp: The standard integrated program includes 30 classroom hours and 6 hours behind the wheel.

q: May a California provisional driver drive for pay?
a: Yes, after six months
d: Yes, for food delivery only
exp: Provisional drivers may not drive for pay or drive vehicles that need a commercial license.

q: You are driving in a California carpool lane when an ambulance with its siren on comes up behind you. What does the law require?
a: Leave the carpool lane when safe, then pull right and stop
b: Stay in the carpool lane, slow down and let it pass
c: Stop in the carpool lane right where you are
d: Pull left onto the median shoulder and stop
exp: Drivers in a carpool or other preferential lane must leave that lane as soon as they safely can, then yield by pulling right.
src: Vehicle Code 21806 (california.public.law); California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 7

q: A fire engine with its siren on comes up behind you on a California one-way street. Where should you pull over?
a: To whichever edge is closer, left or right
b: To the right edge, clear of any intersection
c: To the left edge, since the street is one-way
d: Stop where you are in your lane
exp: California law sends you to the right-hand edge or curb, clear of any intersection, and gives no different rule for one-way streets.
src: Vehicle Code 21806 (california.public.law); California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 7

q: What can happen if you drive to the scene of a fire or crash in California just to watch?
a: Nothing, if you stay in your car
d: Only a fine, if you block a lane
exp: Driving to a fire, collision or other disaster scene gets in the way of emergency crews and can lead to arrest.

q: Rain makes you run your windshield wipers nonstop during the day in California. What must you do?
a: Turn on your parking lights only
d: Nothing until 30 minutes after sunset
exp: When wipers are in continuous use because of rain, fog or snow, California requires low-beam headlights.
src: Vehicle Code 24400(b); California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 5

q: Is it legal in California to drive at dusk with only your parking lights on?
a: No, parking lights alone are illegal
d: Yes, if your daytime running lights work
exp: The handbook says it is illegal to drive using only parking lights; use headlights.

q: A California officer signals you to stop while you are in the carpool lane. Where should you stop?
a: In the carpool lane
c: On the left shoulder next to the carpool lane
d: At the next exit ramp, however far
exp: Move completely onto the right shoulder, even from the carpool lane, and stop in a well-lit spot if you can.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 6, Law Enforcement Stops

q: During a California traffic stop, which documents must the driver produce?
a: License and registration, but not insurance
b: License and a passport or other photo ID
c: License, proof of insurance and registration
d: Proof of insurance and the vehicle title
exp: The driver of a stopped vehicle must produce a driver's license, proof of insurance and registration.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 6, Your Rights During the Enforcement Stop

q: Under California law, when must an officer tell you the reason for a traffic stop?
a: When you ask, after the questions are done
b: Before questioning you, except in an emergency
c: Never; the reason appears on the ticket
d: After writing the ticket, before you leave
exp: Officers must state the reason for the stop before questioning, unless withholding it is needed to protect life or property from an immediate threat.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 6, Law Enforcement Stops

q: A 19-year-old drives alone in California with a sealed six-pack in the trunk. Which is true?
a: It is illegal unless an allowed adult is along
b: It is legal because the cans are sealed
c: It is legal if the alcohol is in the trunk
d: It is illegal only if the driver has been drinking
exp: A driver under 21 may not knowingly carry alcohol unless accompanied by a parent, guardian, responsible adult relative or an adult the parent named, or while working for a licensee.

q: A 20-year-old uses a fake ID to buy beer in California for the first time. What is the penalty?
a: At least $100, or 8 to 12 hours of service
b: At least $250, or 24 to 32 hours of service
c: A $50 fine and no other penalty
d: The store is fined, but not the buyer
exp: Using false ID to buy alcohol under 21 is a misdemeanor: at least $250, 24 to 32 hours of community service, or both.

q: A 16-year-old with no license yet is convicted of riding a bicycle under the influence in California. What can happen?
a: Nothing, since it was a bicycle
b: A $25 fine, with no license effect
c: A one-year delay in getting a license
d: A 30-day delay in getting a license
exp: A person 13 to 20 convicted of bicycling under the influence may have the driving privilege suspended or delayed for one year.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 9; Vehicle Code 13202.5

q: At what point total can DMV treat an adult California driver as a negligent operator?
a: 3 in 12 months, 5 in 24 or 7 in 36
d: 4 in 12 months, 6 in 24 or 8 in 36
exp: An adult license may be suspended at 4 points in 12 months, 6 in 24 months or 8 in 36 months.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 7, Points on Your Driver's Record; Vehicle Code 12810.5

q: How many points does a DUI conviction count on a California driving record?
a: 2 points
d: 6 points
exp: DUI, hit-and-run and reckless driving count 2 points; most other moving violations count 1.

q: A California judge offers traffic violator school for a 1-point ticket. What does finishing it do?
a: Removes the ticket from your record entirely
b: Keeps the ticket from your insurance company
c: Erases all points from the past 3 years
d: Lets you skip paying any fine
exp: The citation is not reported to your insurer but stays on your record. You may do this once in any 18-month period.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 7, Traffic Violator School

q: How often may a California driver use traffic violator school for a 1-point ticket?
a: Once a year
d: As often as the judge allows
exp: Traffic violator school for a 1-point violation is allowed once in any 18-month period.
src: California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Section 7, Traffic Violator School

q: You are stopped at a red light on a one-way street, and the cross street is two-way. May you turn left on red in California?
a: No, only onto another one-way street
b: Yes, without stopping, if no cars are coming
c: Yes, but only if a sign allows it
d: Yes, after a full stop and yielding
exp: A left turn on red is allowed only from a one-way street onto another one-way street.
src: Vehicle Code 21453; California Driver's Handbook (DL 600, 2025), Sections 6 and 7
